title: E/M Coding Level Calculator
problem: Family medicine physicians see 15-20 patients daily and must assign correct E/M (Evaluation and Management) CPT codes for each encounter. Undercoding loses revenue ($20-50 per visit), overcoding triggers audits and fraud penalties. Manually determining the correct level based on medical decision-making complexity, time, and documentation is tedious and error-prone.
who: All family medicine physicians, especially early-career and employed physicians

skill_spec.name: E/M Code Level Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Determines correct E/M CPT code level based on visit complexity, medical decision-making, and time spent

inputs.name: problem_severity
inputs.label: Highest problem severity (minimal / low / moderate / high)

inputs.name: data_reviewed
inputs.label: Amount of data reviewed (minimal / limited / moderate / extensive)

inputs.name: risk_level
inputs.label: Risk of complications (minimal / low / moderate / high)

skill_spec.formula_hint: MDM determined by 2-of-3 rule: problems, data, risk. Time-based coding uses total time thresholds: 99212=10-19min, 99213=20-29min, 99214=30-39min, 99215=40-54min. Higher of MDM-based or time-based code applies.

example_queries: I saw an established patient with 3 chronic conditions, reviewed outside records and labs, moderate risk — what code?
Spent 45 minutes total on a complex new patient visit, what E/M level should I bill?

title: RVU and Compensation Calculator
problem: Family physicians in employed settings are compensated based on work RVUs (Relative Value Units). Tracking productivity, understanding how each visit type contributes to RVU targets, and projecting annual compensation requires complex calculations across different CPT codes and conversion factors. Many physicians don't realize they're leaving money on the table until year-end reconciliation.
who: Employed family physicians with RVU-based compensation

skill_spec.name: RVU Productivity & Compensation Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates work RVUs from visit mix and projects annual compensation based on conversion factor

inputs.name: visits_99203
inputs.label: Number of new patient 99203 visits per week

inputs.name: visits_99204
inputs.label: Number of new patient 99204 visits per week

skill_spec.formula_hint: wRVU per CPT: 99213=1.30, 99214=1.92, 99215=2.80, 99203=1.60, 99204=2.60. Weekly wRVU = sum(visits * wRVU_each). Annual = weekly * weeks_worked. Compensation = annual_wrvus * conversion_factor. National median conversion factor ~$55-65/RVU for FM.

example_queries: I see 12 99213s, 5 99214s, and 2 new patients per week at $58/RVU. What's my projected annual comp?
I need to hit 4,800 RVUs this year. I'm at 2,100 through May — am I on track?

title: MIPS Score Estimator
problem: Family physicians must report MIPS (Merit-based Incentive Payment System) quality measures annually or face Medicare payment adjustments of up to -9%. Calculating the composite score across Quality, Improvement Activities, Promoting Interoperability, and Cost categories is confusing. Many small practices lose thousands in reimbursement due to poor MIPS performance they didn't track proactively.
who: All Medicare-participating family physicians, especially small/independent practices

skill_spec.name: MIPS Composite Score Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Estimates MIPS composite score and projected Medicare payment adjustment from category scores

inputs.name: quality_points
inputs.label: Quality category points earned (out of 70 max)

inputs.name: ia_activities
inputs.label: Number of Improvement Activities completed (high-weighted count double)

outputs.name: dollar_impact
outputs.label: Estimated dollar impact on Medicare revenue

skill_spec.formula_hint: Composite = Quality(30%)*quality_pct + Cost(30%)*cost_pct + PI(25%)*pi_pct + IA(15%)*ia_pct. Quality_pct = points/max_points. IA: need 40 points (high=20, medium=10). Performance threshold ~75 points for neutral adjustment. Exceptional bonus above 89.

example_queries: I reported 6 quality measures averaging 8 points each, did 4 improvement activities, and got 85 on Promoting Interoperability. What's my MIPS score?
My MIPS composite score is 45 — how much will I lose on Medicare payments?

title: Prior Authorization Request Generator
problem: Family physicians spend an average of 14 hours per week on prior authorizations. Each PA requires specific clinical justification language that matches insurer criteria. Denied PAs delay patient care and require time-consuming appeals. Having a properly structured PA letter with medical necessity language dramatically increases approval rates.
who: All family medicine physicians and their office staff

skill_spec.name: Prior Authorization Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates a prior authorization request letter with medical necessity justification for medications, procedures, and referrals

variables.name: prior_treatments
variables.label: Prior treatments tried and failed (step therapy)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (physician info, date, insurer) -> Patient demographics -> Diagnosis and clinical history -> Medical necessity statement -> Prior treatments tried/failed (step therapy documentation) -> Specific request with CPT/HCPCS/NDC codes -> Supporting evidence/guidelines -> Urgency statement if applicable -> Physician signature block

example_queries: Write a prior auth letter for Ozempic for a type 2 diabetic who failed metformin and glipizide, BMI 34
Generate PA request for MRI lumbar spine, patient with 6 weeks of radiculopathy not responding to PT and NSAIDs

title: Chronic Care Management Billing Checklist
problem: Chronic Care Management (CCM) codes (99490, 99491, 99487) represent significant additional revenue ($42-$130+ per patient per month) but require specific documentation, time tracking, and patient consent. Many family physicians leave this revenue on the table because the requirements seem complex. Those who bill CCM improperly face audit risk and clawbacks.
who: Family physicians managing patients with 2+ chronic conditions

skill_spec.name: CCM Billing Compliance Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step checklist ensuring proper documentation and billing for Chronic Care Management services
steps: Step 1: Confirm patient has 2+ chronic conditions expected to last 12+ months
Step 2: Obtain and document verbal or written patient consent for CCM (required before first billing)
Step 3: Confirm only one provider is billing CCM for this patient this month
Step 4: Create or update comprehensive care plan in EHR
Step 5: Track non-face-to-face clinical staff time (minimum 20 minutes for 99490)
Step 6: Document all care coordination activities with dates and times
Step 7: Ensure 24/7 access to care team is available to patient
Step 8: For complex CCM (99487): verify 60+ minutes of clinical staff time
Step 9: Submit claim with appropriate ICD-10 codes for qualifying chronic conditions
Step 10: Verify no same-day billing conflicts with TCM or other care management codes
warnings: Warning: Patient consent must be documented BEFORE first CCM billing — retroactive consent is not valid
Warning: Only ONE practitioner can bill CCM per patient per calendar month
Warning: Time spent during face-to-face visits does NOT count toward CCM time requirements
Warning: General supervision required — billing physician must be available, not necessarily present

example_queries: What do I need to document to bill CCM 99490 for a diabetic/hypertensive patient?
Can I bill CCM and TCM in the same month for the same patient?

title: Medication Dosage and Interaction Checker
problem: Family physicians prescribe across all organ systems and age groups, managing complex polypharmacy in elderly patients. Calculating weight-based pediatric doses, renal-adjusted doses, and checking multi-drug interactions across a patient's full medication list is high-stakes work. A missed interaction or dosing error can result in adverse events and malpractice claims.
who: All family medicine physicians, especially those managing elderly patients with polypharmacy

skill_spec.name: Dosage Calculator & Interaction Checker
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates weight-based and renal-adjusted medication doses and flags common dangerous interactions
skill_spec.formula_hint: Pediatric dose = weight_kg * mg_per_kg_per_day / doses_per_day. Renal adjustment: CrCl 30-60 reduce by 50%, CrCl <30 reduce by 75% (drug-specific). Flag interactions by class: ACEi+K-sparing=hyperkalemia, warfarin+NSAID=bleeding, statin+macrolide=rhabdomyolysis.

example_queries: What's the amoxicillin dose for a 22kg child with otitis media?
Patient on warfarin, metoprolol, lisinopril, and amlodipine — I want to add azithromycin. Any interactions?

problem: Family physicians must track age-specific and risk-based preventive screening recommendations from USPSTF, CDC, ACIP, and ACS. Guidelines update frequently (e.g., lung cancer screening expanded in 2021, anxiety screening added 2023). Missing a recommended screening exposes patients to harm and the physician to malpractice risk. It also impacts MIPS quality measures.
who: All family medicine physicians performing annual wellness visits

skill_spec.name: Preventive Care Screening Schedule
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of age/sex/risk-appropriate preventive screenings based on current USPSTF and CDC guidelines
skill_spec.data_domain: USPSTF, CDC, ACIP, and ACS preventive care recommendations for primary care

data_hints.source_law: USPSTF A/B recommendations, Affordable Care Act Section 2713

example_queries: What screenings are due for a 52-year-old female with no significant history?
When should I start lung cancer screening? Patient is 55, smoked 1 pack/day for 25 years, quit 3 years ago

title: SOAP Note Generator
problem: Family physicians spend 1-2 hours after clinic completing documentation. Each encounter requires a structured SOAP note with proper medical terminology, assessment, and plan that supports the E/M code billed. Poor documentation leads to audit failures, denied claims, and malpractice vulnerability. This is the #1 driver of physician burnout.
who: All family medicine physicians, especially those without AI scribes

skill_spec.name: SOAP Note Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates structured SOAP encounter notes from key clinical inputs that support proper E/M coding

variables.name: visit_type
variables.label: Visit type (follow-up / new patient / AWV / well-child)

variables.name: hpi_elements
variables.label: HPI key elements (onset, location, duration, severity, context)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Subjective (CC, HPI, ROS, PMH/PSH/FH/SH) -> Objective (Vitals, Physical Exam by system) -> Assessment (numbered problem list with ICD-10) -> Plan (per problem: medications, labs, imaging, referrals, patient education, follow-up timeline) -> Time statement if billing by time

example_queries: Generate a SOAP note for a 58-year-old male follow-up for uncontrolled type 2 diabetes, A1c 8.9, currently on metformin 1000mg BID
Write an encounter note for a well-child visit, 4-year-old, routine immunizations due

title: HIPAA Breach Response Checklist
problem: Family medicine practices handle thousands of patient records and a single HIPAA breach can cost $50,000+ per incident. When a potential breach occurs (lost laptop, misdirected fax, staff accessing records improperly), physicians often don't know the required response timeline or notification obligations. The 60-day notification rule and state-specific requirements add complexity.
who: Practice owners, medical directors, and privacy officers in family medicine practices

skill_spec.name: HIPAA Breach Response Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step breach response checklist with notification timelines and documentation requirements
steps: Step 1: Identify and contain the breach immediately — stop ongoing disclosure, recover data if possible
Step 2: Document discovery date (this starts the 60-day clock for notifications)
Step 3: Conduct risk assessment: nature of PHI, who accessed it, whether it was actually acquired/viewed, extent of mitigation
Step 4: Apply the 4-factor test to determine if breach exception applies (unintentional, authorized person, unable to retain)
Step 5: If breach confirmed — notify affected individuals within 60 days of discovery (written notice)
Step 6: If 500+ individuals affected — notify HHS immediately and local media
Step 7: If fewer than 500 — log and report to HHS annually (by March 1 of following year)
Step 8: Check state breach notification laws (may have shorter timelines than HIPAA)
Step 9: Document all response actions and corrective measures taken
Step 10: Update HIPAA policies and provide staff retraining to prevent recurrence
warnings: Warning: The 60-day clock starts at DISCOVERY, not when investigation concludes
Warning: Failure to notify HHS for 500+ person breaches can result in separate penalties
Warning: State laws may require faster notification (e.g., California: 15 days for some entities)
Warning: Business associates must notify covered entity within 60 days of discovering breach

example_queries: A staff member accessed a patient record without authorization — is this a reportable HIPAA breach?
We sent lab results to the wrong patient by fax — what do we need to do?

title: Disability and FMLA Documentation Generator
problem: Family physicians frequently complete disability certifications, FMLA paperwork, and return-to-work forms. These forms require specific functional limitation language that matches legal definitions. Improperly completed forms delay patient benefits, generate rework, and can expose the physician to liability if language is too vague or too definitive.
who: All family medicine physicians seeing working-age adults

skill_spec.name: Disability & FMLA Form Completion Guide
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates functional limitation language and clinical justification for disability, FMLA, and return-to-work documentation

variables.name: form_type
variables.label: Form type (FMLA / short-term disability / long-term disability / ADA accommodation / return-to-work)

variables.name: functional_limitations
variables.label: Specific functional limitations (lifting, standing, sitting, cognitive)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Patient identification -> Diagnosis and clinical findings -> Specific functional limitations (use measurable terms: 'cannot lift >10 lbs', 'cannot stand >30 min') -> Treatment plan and prognosis -> Expected duration -> Work restrictions with specificity -> Physician attestation

example_queries: Help me fill out FMLA certification for a patient with major depression who can't work full days
Write disability language for a patient with lumbar disc herniation — what functional limitations should I document?

Physicians often don't know whether specific clinical scenarios put them at elevated legal risk or what documentation practices protect them. Average malpractice payout for family medicine exceeds $300,000.
who: All family medicine physicians, especially early-career and those in high-risk states

skill_spec.name: Malpractice Risk Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Analyzes clinical scenarios for malpractice risk and recommends documentation and follow-up practices to mitigate liability
skill_spec.expertise_area: Medical malpractice risk assessment and mitigation for family medicine

I found an incidental lung nodule on chest X-ray. What's my follow-up obligation and liability if I miss tracking it?

Missing deadlines risks license lapse or board certification expiration. Requirements vary significantly by state.

title: Annual Wellness Visit (AWV) Documentation Checklist
problem: The Medicare Annual Wellness Visit is a key revenue and quality opportunity but has specific required elements that differ from a standard physical exam. Many family physicians confuse AWV with a regular annual physical, leading to denied claims or missed billing opportunities. Properly structured AWVs also feed MIPS quality measures and HCC risk adjustment coding.

skill_spec.name: Medicare AWV Documentation Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Ensures all required elements of Initial and Subsequent Annual Wellness Visits are documented for clean billing
steps: Step 1: Verify patient eligibility (Medicare Part B, 12+ months since Welcome to Medicare or last AWV)
Step 2: Update Health Risk Assessment (HRA) questionnaire — required element
Step 3: Review and update medical/surgical history and family history
Step 4: Update current medications and providers list
Step 5: Measure height, weight, BMI, blood pressure
Step 6: Assess cognitive function (observation or structured tool)
Step 7: Screen for depression (PHQ-2 or PHQ-9)
Step 8: Assess functional ability and safety (fall risk, ADL/IADL)
Step 9: Update personalized prevention plan with screening schedule
Step 10: Provide advance care planning discussion if appropriate (bill G0505 separately)
Step 11: Capture all active diagnoses for HCC coding — review problem list thoroughly
Step 12: Bill G0438 (Initial AWV) or G0439 (Subsequent AWV) — do NOT bill with 99213-99215 for same problems
warnings: Warning: AWV is NOT a head-to-toe physical exam — avoid documenting it as such
Warning: Do NOT bill E/M and AWV for the same conditions — separate modifier-25 E/M only for distinct new problems
Warning: Health Risk Assessment is REQUIRED — missing HRA = denied claim
Warning: HCC coding during AWV directly impacts practice's risk-adjusted revenue in value-based contracts

example_queries: What elements are required for a subsequent Medicare Annual Wellness Visit?
Can I bill a 99214 on the same day as an AWV?
